summary:
Congressional restrictions on D.C.'s budget and operations continue to affect the District's institutions and governance, while advocates are intensifying statehood efforts heading into the midterm elections and beyond. The presence of National Guard troops in D.C. remains a point of contention as civil liberties organizations demand withdrawal, and statehood supporters are working to build momentum both locally and nationally.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
